subject: Recap + Joint Execution Checklist — Redwood x Asterion
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rao <maya.rao@asterion.com>, Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@asterion.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-17T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + Joint Execution Checklist — Redwood x Asterion

Hi Maya / Thomas —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and a proposed "joint execution checklist" to make next steps explicit so we keep momentum. I pulled this from our call notes and the actions we agreed on. Please review and either confirm or suggest adjustments (owners/dates).

Key pains you described
- Per-call: inference costs have ballooned with current vendor (50–70% over forecast) and there's limited visibility into token-level spend.
- Latency: embedding and rerank flows occasionally spike > 500ms p95, affecting search relevance SLAs.
- Data residency: some PII-derived metadata must remain in us-east region for compliance.

Success criteria / goals we heard
- Reduce end-to-end per-request inference cost by ~40–50% in pilot.
- Achieve p95 latency < 200ms for embedding + rerank at 90% of production traffic.
- Confirm deployment that meets Asterion's regional data controls and SOC2 evidence for security review.

Proposed joint checklist (owners and target dates)
1) Pilot scope & acceptance tests — Owner: Soojin (Redwood) / Maya (Asterion); Target: 2026-10-01
2) Pilot infra & VPC setup (data residency confirmation) — Owner: Laura (Redwood Infra) / Priya (Asterion Legal/IT); Target: 2026-10-07
3) Cost estimate & quantization profile — Owner: Ben (Redwood Solutions); Target: 2026-09-24
4) Security package (SOC2 evidence, network diagrams) — Owner: Laura (Redwood) / Priya (Asterion); Target: 2026-09-28
5) Procurement & contract window — Owner: Thomas (Asterion Procurement) / Soojin (Redwood Sales); Target: 2026-10-15
6) Pilot go/no-go decision (exec approval) — Owner: Thomas / Maya; Target: 2026-10-20

Ask items for Asterion (please confirm)
- Point of contact for procurement and expected approval cadence
- Any additional compliance artifacts beyond SOC2 we should surface now
- Confirmation that the acceptance test matrix above reflects your expectations

Attachments: redwood-asterion-exec-checklist-v1.xlsx (one-page milestones + owners) — I uploaded a working copy to the Drive link below and will iterate on the dates once we hear back.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Asterion-Redwood-Exec (working doc)
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-ASTR-2026-09

If that looks good, I propose a short 20-minute sync next week (Tue or Wed) to lock owners and procurement timeline.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai

From: Maya Rao <maya.rao@asterion.com>

Date: 2026-09-18T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + Joint Execution Checklist — Redwood x Asterion

Soojin —

Appreciate the thorough recap. High level — this matches our view. A couple of small updates:
- Procurement owner will be Thomas, but heads-up: legal (Priya) typically requires 2 weeks for initial contract review and another 1–2 weeks to sign after commercial terms are agreed.
- For the security package, Priya asked if you can include a sample data flow diagram that shows where PII will be redacted/kept in-region.
- Acceptance tests look good — add an availability target (99.5% monthly) to the pilot acceptance criteria if possible.

I'll confirm availability for a short sync on Tue (Sep 22) afternoon; Thomas is traveling but will join remotely if we lock a time.

Best,
Maya Rao
Head of ML Products, Asterion Financial
maya.rao@asterion.com

Hi Maya / Thomas / Priya —

Thanks for the quick turn. Attached is v2 of the joint milestones (redwood-asterion-joint-milestones-v2.xlsx) with the changes requested: procurement owner updated to Thomas, added availability target (99.5%), and a placeholder for the data flow diagram.

- Ben will deliver cost + perf table by 2026-09-24 (Ben action).
- Laura to upload SOC2 artifact bundle and a first-pass data flow diagram by 2026-09-28 (Laura action).
- Please confirm procurement review window: Maya mentioned 2 weeks for legal + 1–2 weeks to finalize after terms. Thomas — can you confirm if that aligns with Asterion's procurement cadence?
- Confirm decision committee members for the 10/20 pilot go/no-go: is it Maya (exec sponsor), Thomas (procurement), plus two engineering leads? If you can reply with names I will add them to the acceptance matrix.

Proposed pilot window: 2026-10-10 -> 2026-10-19 with formal go/no-go on 2026-10-20. This gives procurement and legal time to complete.

Next step: if that schedule looks reasonable, can we lock the Tue Sep 22 sync (11:00 PT) to finalize owners and the contract timeline? I will send a calendar invite with an agenda.
